questions.q: The set $\{x : x \text{ is a distinct letter in the word 'ALLOWED'}\}$ has how many elements?
questions.explanation: The distinct letters are A, L, O, W, E, D — 6 elements (the repeated L is counted once).
questions.trick: Count each repeated letter only once.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A = \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ and $B = \{4,5,6,7\}$, then $n(A \triangle B)$ is
questions.explanation: $A - B = \{1,2,3\}$ and $B - A = \{6,7\}$, so $A\triangle B = \{1,2,3,6,7\}$, which has 5 elements.
questions.trick: Symmetric difference count: add elements unique to each set.
questions.subject: maths

questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In a class of 60 students, 25 play cricket, 20 play football and 10 play both. The number of students who play neither game is
questions.trick: Neither $=$ total $- n(A\cup B)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of proper subsets of a set containing 5 elements is
questions.explanation: $2^5 - 1 = 31$ (the set itself is excluded).
questions.trick: Proper subsets $= 2^n - 1$; exclude the set itself.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $n(A) = 3$ and $n(B) = 4$, the number of relations from $A$ to $B$ is
questions.explanation: A relation is a subset of $A\times B$, which has 12 elements; number of subsets $= 2^{12}$.
questions.trick: Relations from $A$ to $B$ $= 2^{n(A)n(B)}$, not $n(A)n(B)$ itself.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If a set $A$ has 64 subsets, then $n(A)$ is
questions.explanation: $2^n = 64 \Rightarrow n = 6$.
questions.trick: Solve $2^n =$ given subset count for $n$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which of the following sets is infinite?
questions.explanation: $\{x : x\in\mathbb N\}$ is the set of all natural numbers, which is infinite; the other three are finite.
questions.trick: $\mathbb N$ itself is infinite; equation-defined sets are usually finite.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq A$, then
questions.explanation: Mutual containment of two sets means they have exactly the same elements, so $A = B$.
questions.trick: Mutual containment $A\subseteq B$ and $B\subseteq A$ forces $A=B$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A$ has 3 elements and $B$ has 2 elements, the number of ways to choose a relation from $A$ to $B$ that is a function is
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 elements of $A$ independently maps to one of 2 elements of $B$: total functions $= 2^3 = 8$.
questions.trick: Functions $A\to B$ (no restriction) $= n(B)^{n(A)}$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $R = \{(x,y) : x, y \in \mathbb{Z}, x^2 + y^2 = 25\}$, the domain of $R$ is
questions.explanation: Integer solutions of $x^2+y^2=25$: $(\pm5,0), (0,\pm5), (\pm3,\pm4), (\pm4,\pm3)$. So $x$ takes values $\{-5,-4,-3,0,3,4,5\}$.
questions.trick: List integer $(x,y)$ pairs on the circle, then collect the $x$-values.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The total number of relations that can be defined from a set $A$ with 2 elements to a set $B$ with 3 elements is
questions.explanation: Number of relations $= 2^{n(A)n(B)} = 2^{2\times3} = 2^6 = 64$.
questions.trick: Relations from $A$ to $B$ $= 2^{n(A)n(B)}$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A = \{1,2\}$ and $B = \{3,4\}$, then $A \times B$ is
questions.explanation: $A\times B$ pairs every element of $A$ (first) with every element of $B$ (second).
questions.trick: $A\times B$: pair every element of $A$ (first) with every $B$ (second).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 2x+1$, then $(f+g)(1)$ equals
questions.trick: $(f+g)(a) = f(a)+g(a)$; evaluate each separately first.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which of the following functions is odd?
questions.explanation: $f(x)=x^3$ satisfies $f(-x) = -f(x)$, so it is odd.
questions.trick: Odd function: $f(-x)=-f(x)$ — pure odd powers of $x$ qualify.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $x$ is in the first quadrant, the value of $\sin 2x$ is
questions.explanation: $x = \pi/4$ (since $\sin x = 1/\sqrt2$ in QI), so $\sin2x = \sin(\pi/2) = 1$.
questions.trick: Identify the standard angle first, then apply $\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\sin(A-B)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: This is the standard angle-difference formula for sine.
questions.trick: $\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$ — memorise the sign pattern.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\sin A = \dfrac35$ (A acute) and $\cos B = \dfrac{5}{13}$ (B acute), the value of $\sin(A+B)$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos A = 4/5$, $\sin B = 12/13$. $\sin(A+B) = \sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B = \dfrac{3}{5}\cdot\dfrac{5}{13}+\dfrac{4}{5}\cdot\dfrac{12}{13} = \dfrac{15+48}{65} = \dfrac{63}{65}$.
questions.trick: Find missing ratios via Pythagoras, then apply $\sin(A+B)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The general solution of $\tan\theta = 1$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\tan$ has period $\pi$ and $\tan\frac{\pi}{4}=1$, the general solution is $\theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $n\in\mathbb Z$.
questions.trick: $\tan\theta=\tan\alpha \Rightarrow \theta=n\pi+\alpha$ (period $\pi$, no $(-1)^n$).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $\sec 60^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos60^\circ = \dfrac12$, so $\sec60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\cos60^\circ} = 2$.
questions.trick: $\sec\theta = 1/\cos\theta$; invert the known cosine value.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A + B = 45^\circ$, the value of $(1+\tan A)(1+\tan B)$ is
questions.explanation: $\tan(A+B)=1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}=1 \Rightarrow \tan A+\tan B = 1-\tan A\tan B$. Expanding $(1+\tan A)(1+\tan B) = 1+\tan A+\tan B+\tan A\tan B = 1+(1-\tan A\tan B)+\tan A\tan B = 2$.
questions.trick: $A+B=45^\circ \Rightarrow (1+\tan A)(1+\tan B)=2$ (standard shortcut).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $\cos(-60^\circ)$ is
questions.explanation: Cosine is an even function, so $\cos(-60^\circ) = \cos60^\circ = \dfrac12$.
questions.trick: Cosine is even: $\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The domain of $\tan x$ excludes values of the form
questions.explanation: $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ is undefined where $\cos x = 0$, i.e. at $x = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
questions.trick: $\tan x$ undefined where $\cos x=0$: $x=(2n+1)\pi/2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The amplitude of $y = 3\sin(2x)$ is
questions.explanation: For $y = a\sin(bx)$, the amplitude is $|a|$, which here is 3.
questions.trick: Amplitude of $a\sin(bx)$ is just $|a|$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $\cot\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = 135^\circ$ lies in the second quadrant, where $\cot$ is negative; $\cot135^\circ = -\cot45^\circ = -1$.
questions.trick: Identify the quadrant of the angle first, then apply the reference-angle sign.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The general solution of $\cos\theta = \cos\alpha$ is
questions.explanation: The standard general solution of $\cos\theta=\cos\alpha$ is $\theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha$, $n\in\mathbb Z$.
questions.trick: $\cos\theta=\cos\alpha \Rightarrow \theta=2n\pi\pm\alpha$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\cos\theta = -\dfrac12$ and $\theta$ lies in the third quadrant, then $\theta$ equals (principal value in $[0,2\pi)$)
questions.explanation: $\cos\theta=-1/2$ gives reference angle $\pi/3$; in quadrant III, $\theta = \pi + \pi/3 = 4\pi/3$.
questions.trick: Quadrant III: reference angle from $\cos$, add $\pi$ to it.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The period of the function $f(x) = \sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ is
questions.explanation: Period of $\sin(kx)$ is $2\pi/k$; here $k=1/2$, so period $= 2\pi/(1/2) = 4\pi$.
questions.trick: Period of $\sin(kx)$ is $2\pi/k$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\sin 50^\circ - \sin 70^\circ + \sin 10^\circ$ equals
questions.explanation: $\sin50^\circ - \sin70^\circ = -2\cos60^\circ\sin10^\circ = -2(1/2)\sin10^\circ = -\sin10^\circ$. Adding $\sin10^\circ$ gives $0$.
questions.trick: Combine the two sines via sum-to-product first; the rest cancels.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In the third quadrant, which of the following trigonometric ratios is positive?
questions.explanation: In the third quadrant, only $\tan\theta$ and $\cot\theta$ are positive; sine, cosine and their reciprocals are negative.
questions.trick: Quadrant III: only tan and cot are positive.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The sum of the roots of $ax^2+bx+c=0$ ($a\ne0$) is
questions.explanation: For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, sum of roots $= -\dfrac{b}{a}$.
questions.trick: Sum of roots $=-b/a$ — read the sign carefully.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For what value of $k$ does $x^2-4x+k=0$ have equal roots?
questions.explanation: Equal roots require $D=0$: $16-4k=0 \Rightarrow k=4$.
questions.trick: Equal roots $\Rightarrow D=0$; solve for the unknown.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The argument of $z = -4$ (a negative real number) is
questions.explanation: $-4$ lies on the negative real axis, which corresponds to argument $\pi$.
questions.trick: Negative real axis $\Rightarrow$ argument $\pi$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Simplify $\dfrac{1}{1+i}$
questions.explanation: Multiply by conjugate: $\dfrac{1}{1+i}\cdot\dfrac{1-i}{1-i} = \dfrac{1-i}{1+1} = \dfrac{1-i}{2}$.
questions.trick: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $z_1 = 1+i$ and $z_2 = 1-i$, then $|z_1 z_2|$ is
questions.trick: $|z_1z_2|=|z_1||z_2|$ — multiply moduli, skip expanding the product.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $-4x \ge 12$, then
questions.explanation: Dividing by $-4$ (negative) flips the sign: $x \le -3$.
questions.trick: Dividing by a negative coefficient flips the inequality.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The solution of $|x+3| > 5$ is
questions.trick: $|x-a|>r \Rightarrow x>a+r$ or $x<a-r$.

questions.q: The solution of $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{x}{3} < 5$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{3x+2x}{6}<5 \Rightarrow \dfrac{5x}{6}<5 \Rightarrow x<6$.
questions.trick: Clear fractions via LCM (positive), then isolate $x$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The solution of $-5x + 10 \le 0$ is
questions.explanation: $-5x \le -10$; dividing by $-5$ flips the inequality: $x \ge 2$.
questions.trick: Dividing by a negative coefficient flips the inequality sign.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For $a<b$ with $a,b$ both negative, which is true?
questions.explanation: For same-sign numbers, taking reciprocals reverses the inequality: $a<b \Rightarrow 1/a>1/b$ (e.g. $a=-3,b=-1$: $1/a=-1/3 > 1/b=-1$).
questions.trick: Same-sign reciprocals flip the inequality direction.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A taxi charges ₹50 plus ₹12 per km. If a passenger has at most ₹200 to spend, the maximum whole number of km they can travel is
questions.explanation: $50+12x\le200 \Rightarrow 12x\le150 \Rightarrow x\le12.5$; the largest whole number of km is 12.
questions.trick: Set up cost $\le$ budget, solve, then floor to a whole number.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of straight lines that can be formed by joining 6 points in a plane, no three of which are collinear, is
questions.explanation: A line needs 2 points: $^6C_2 = 15$.
questions.trick: A line needs 2 points, order irrelevant $\Rightarrow ^nC_2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $^{10}C_4 + {}^{10}C_5$ is
questions.trick: Pascal's rule: $^nC_{r-1}+{}^nC_r = {}^{n+1}C_r$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In how many ways can a committee of 3 men and 2 women be formed from 5 men and 4 women?
questions.explanation: Choose men and women independently and multiply: $^5C_3 \times {}^4C_2 = 10\times6 = 60$.
questions.trick: Split by group, choose each independently, then multiply.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Out of 6 novels and 3 biographies, the number of ways to choose 4 novels and 1 biography is
questions.trick: Choose each category independently with $^nC_r$, then multiply.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In how many ways can 8 people be seated in a row if 4 particular people must always sit together?
questions.explanation: Treat the 4 people as one block: this gives 5 units to arrange in $5!$ ways, and the block internally in $4!$ ways: $5!\times4! = 120\times24 = 2880$.
questions.trick: Glue the 'together' group into one block: arrange blocks $\times$ internal order.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of ways to distribute 5 distinct books to 5 students, one each, is
questions.explanation: This is arranging 5 distinct books among 5 students: $5! = 120$.
questions.trick: Distributing $n$ distinct items to $n$ people, one each, is just $n!$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $^8P_3$ is
questions.trick: $^nP_r = n(n-1)\cdots$ for $r$ terms; multiply straight down.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of diagonals of a polygon with $n$ sides is given by the formula
questions.explanation: Total line segments between $n$ vertices are $^nC_2 = \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$; removing the $n$ sides gives $\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$ diagonals.
questions.trick: Diagonals of an $n$-gon $= n(n-3)/2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: How many 4-letter codes can be formed from the 26 English letters if repetition is not allowed?
questions.trick: No repetition, order matters $\Rightarrow ^nP_r$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using digits $1,2,3,4,5$ without repetition?
questions.explanation: $^5P_3 = 5\times4\times3 = 60$.
questions.trick: No repetition, order matters $\Rightarrow$ use $^nP_r$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In the expansion of $(1+x)^{n}$, if the coefficients of the 5th and 6th terms are in the ratio $1:2$, given $^nC_4 : {}^nC_5 = 1:2$, then $n$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{^nC_4}{^nC_5} = \dfrac{5}{n-4} = \dfrac12 \Rightarrow n-4=10 \Rightarrow n=14$.
questions.trick: Set up $^nC_{r}/{}^nC_{r+1}$ ratio equation and solve for $n$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The coefficient of $y^3$ in the expansion of $(2-y)^5$ is
questions.trick: Track $(-1)^r$ sign and the base's power together in $T_{r+1}$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $^nC_4 = {}^nC_6$, then $^nC_2$ equals
questions.explanation: $^nC_4={}^nC_6 \Rightarrow n=4+6=10$ (since $r_1\ne r_2$). Then $^{10}C_2 = 45$.
questions.trick: $^nC_4={}^nC_6 \Rightarrow n=4+6=10$, then compute the target directly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In the expansion of $(1+x)^{20}$, comparing the coefficients of $x^{10}$ and $x^{11}$,
questions.explanation: Since $n=20$ is even, the coefficients $^{20}C_r$ are largest at $r=10$ (the middle term) and decrease moving away from it, so $^{20}C_{10} > {}^{20}C_{11}$.
questions.trick: Even $n$: coefficients peak at the middle index and decrease outward.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which of the following statements about binomial coefficients $^nC_r$ is TRUE?
questions.explanation: The symmetry property $^nC_r = {}^nC_{n-r}$ always holds; the other statements are false in general (e.g. $^nC_0=1$, not $n$).
questions.trick: $^nC_r={}^nC_{n-r}$ is the one universally true symmetry — check that first.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If the sum of the coefficients in the expansion of $(x+y)^n$ is 128, the value of $n$ is
questions.explanation: Putting $x=y=1$ gives $2^n = 128 = 2^7$, so $n=7$.
questions.trick: Put $x=y=1$: sum of coefficients $=2^n$, solve for $n$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: 128 is which term of the GP $2, 4, 8, \ldots$?
questions.trick: $r^{n-1}=\text{term}/\text{first}$; match powers of $r$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which term of the AP $21, 18, 15, \ldots$ is $-81$?
questions.explanation: $a=21, d=-3$; $21-3(n-1)=-81 \Rightarrow n-1=34 \Rightarrow n=35$.
questions.trick: Set $a+(n-1)d=\text{value}$ and solve for $n$ — watch the sign of $d$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $a, b, c$ are in GP, then $\log a, \log b, \log c$ are in
questions.explanation: GP gives $b^2 = ac$, so $2\log b = \log a + \log c$, which is the AP condition.
questions.trick: GP's constant ratio becomes a constant difference after taking $\log$ — that's AP.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Using the sum of an infinite GP, the recurring decimal $0.\overline{3}$ equals
questions.trick: Repeating decimal is a GP with $r=1/10^{\text{digits}}$; sum $=a/(1-r)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In a harmonic progression, the 4th term is $\dfrac12$ and the 8th term is $\dfrac14$. The first term of the HP is
questions.explanation: Reciprocals form an AP: 4th term $=2$, 8th term $=4$, so $d=\dfrac{4-2}{4}=0.5$ and first term $=2-3(0.5)=0.5$. The HP's first term is the reciprocal, $1/0.5=2$.
questions.trick: Invert HP terms into AP, solve there, then invert the answer back.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: An AP has first term 5, last term 45, and sum 400. The number of terms is
questions.explanation: $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l) \Rightarrow 400=\dfrac{n}{2}(50) \Rightarrow n=16$.
questions.trick: $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$ — solve directly for $n$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The equation of the line with slope 0 passing through $(4,-5)$ is
questions.explanation: Slope 0 means a horizontal line: $y=-5$.
questions.trick: Slope 0 means horizontal line: $y=$ given $y$-coordinate.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The tangent of the angle between two lines with slopes 2 and 3 is
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{3-2}{1+2\times3}\right|=\dfrac{1}{7}$.
questions.trick: $\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1m_2}\right|$ — direct formula, no angle needed.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The equation of the line with $x$-intercept 4 and $y$-intercept $-3$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{x}{4}+\dfrac{y}{-3}=1$. Multiplying by 12: $3x-4y=12$, i.e. $3x-4y-12=0$.
questions.trick: Intercept form $x/a+y/b=1$ with given $a,b$; clear denominators.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The line through the intersection of $x+2y-3=0$ and $2x-y+1=0$, passing through the origin, is
questions.explanation: Family: $(x+2y-3)+\lambda(2x-y+1)=0$. At $(0,0)$: $-3+\lambda=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=3$. This gives $7x-y=0$, i.e. $y=7x$.
questions.trick: Family $L_1+\lambda L_2=0$; plug the extra point to find $\lambda$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The lines $2x+3y=5$ and $3x-2y=7$ are
questions.explanation: Slopes are $-2/3$ and $3/2$; product $=-1$, so the lines are perpendicular.
questions.trick: Compute $m_1m_2$; $=-1$ means perpendicular.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The equation of the line through the origin and $(5,5)$ is
questions.explanation: Slope $=\dfrac{5-0}{5-0}=1$, and it passes through the origin, so $y=x$.
questions.trick: Line through origin: $y=mx$ with $m=$ slope to the given point.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A hyperbola has foci $(\pm5,0)$ and transverse axis length 6. Its eccentricity is
questions.explanation: $2a=6 \Rightarrow a=3$; $c=5$; $e=c/a=5/3$.
questions.trick: $e=c/a$; transverse axis gives $a$, foci give $c$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The length of the minor axis of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{49}+\dfrac{y^2}{25}=1$ is
questions.explanation: $a=7, b=5$ (major axis along $x$); minor axis $=2b=10$.
questions.trick: Minor axis $=2b$, $b$ = smaller semi-axis.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The eccentricity of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$ is
questions.trick: $e=c/a$ with $c^2=a^2-b^2$; bigger denominator is $a^2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The length of the conjugate axis of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{25}-\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$ is
questions.explanation: $b^2=9 \Rightarrow b=3$; conjugate axis $=2b=6$.
questions.trick: Conjugate axis $=2b$, $b^2$ under the negative term.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: An ellipse has eccentricity $3/5$ and the distance between its foci is 6. Its major axis has length
questions.explanation: $2c=6 \Rightarrow c=3$; $e=c/a \Rightarrow a=c/e=3\div(3/5)=5$. Major axis $=2a=10$.
questions.trick: $2c=$ given, $a=c/e$; major axis $=2a$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which of the following is a rectangular hyperbola?
questions.explanation: A rectangular hyperbola has $a=b$; $x^2-y^2=16$ can be written as $\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$, so $a=b=4$.
questions.trick: Rectangular hyperbola needs $a=b$; check if both denominators are equal.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two lines have direction ratios proportional to $(1,-2,1)$ and $(2,3,4)$. The lines are
questions.explanation: $1(2)+(-2)(3)+1(4) = 2-6+4=0$, so the lines are perpendicular.
questions.trick: Dot product of dr's $=0$ means perpendicular.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The distance between the points $(0,3,-2)$ and $(0,-1,1)$ is
questions.trick: $d=\sqrt{(\Delta x)^2+(\Delta y)^2+(\Delta z)^2}$; here $\Delta x=0$ drops out.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The distance between the points $(1,2,3)$ and $(4,6,3)$ is
questions.trick: $d=\sqrt{(\Delta x)^2+(\Delta y)^2+(\Delta z)^2}$ — just extend Pythagoras to 3D.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A line has direction ratios $2,5,-4$. Taking $l,m,n$ as its direction cosines (positive magnitude), $l+m+n$ equals
questions.explanation: Magnitude $=\sqrt{4+25+16}=\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt5$; $l+m+n=\dfrac{2+5-4}{3\sqrt5}=\dfrac{3}{3\sqrt5}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}$.
questions.trick: Find magnitude first, then sum the dc's over that one magnitude.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The direction ratios of the $x$-axis are
questions.explanation: The $x$-axis points purely in the $x$-direction, so its direction ratios are $(1,0,0)$.
questions.trick: $x$-axis direction ratios are simply $(1,0,0)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The direction cosines of the $z$-axis are
questions.explanation: The $z$-axis points purely in the $z$-direction, so its direction cosines are $(0,0,1)$.
questions.trick: $z$-axis direction cosines are simply $(0,0,1)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\lim\limits_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{2x^3+3x^2+1}{x^4+5x+2}$ equals
questions.explanation: The denominator's degree (4) exceeds the numerator's degree (3), so dividing by $x^4$ shows the limit is 0.
questions.trick: Denominator's degree $>$ numerator's degree at $\infty$ $\Rightarrow$ limit is 0.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{1-\cos4x}{1-\cos2x}$ equals
questions.explanation: $1-\cos4x=2\sin^22x$ and $1-\cos2x=2\sin^2x$, so the ratio $=\dfrac{\sin^22x}{\sin^2x}=\dfrac{4\sin^2x\cos^2x}{\sin^2x}=4\cos^2x \to 4$ as $x\to0$.
questions.trick: Convert both to $2\sin^2$ form; ratio reduces to $4\cos^2x\to4$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Using first principles, the derivative of $f(x)=x^2$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{(x+h)^2-x^2}{h}=\lim\limits_{h\to0}(2x+h)=2x$.
questions.trick: First-principles for $x^2$ always gives $2x$ — memorize the pattern.

questions.q: $\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{3^x-1}{x}$ equals
questions.explanation: Just as $\dfrac{e^x-1}{x}\to1$, in general $\dfrac{a^x-1}{x}\to\ln a$; here $a=3$, giving $\ln3$.
questions.trick: $(a^x-1)/x\to\ln a$ — generalizes the $e^x$ result.

questions.q: The value of $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}\right)$ at $x=0$ is
questions.explanation: Quotient rule: $\dfrac{(1)(x+1)-(x-1)(1)}{(x+1)^2}=\dfrac{2}{(x+1)^2}$; at $x=0$, this is $2$.
questions.trick: Quotient rule gives a constant-over-square form; plug in the point directly.

questions.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(5)$ equals

questions.q: $\lim\limits_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{3x^2+2x+1}{5x^2-x+7}$ equals
questions.explanation: For equal degree polynomials, the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients: $3/5$.
questions.trick: Equal-degree polynomials at $\infty$: limit = ratio of leading coefficients.

questions.q: $\lim\limits_{x\to3}\dfrac{x^3-27}{x-3}$ equals
questions.explanation: Using $\lim\dfrac{x^n-a^n}{x-a}=na^{n-1}$: $3(3)^2=27$.

questions.q: The value of $\dfrac{d}{dx}(7x^3-2x+9)$ at $x=0$ is
questions.explanation: Derivative $=21x^2-2$; at $x=0$, this equals $-2$.
questions.trick: Differentiate term by term, then substitute the given $x$.

questions.q: For 5 observations with mean 10, the sum of squared deviations from the mean is 50. The standard deviation is
questions.explanation: Variance $=\dfrac{50}{5}=10$, so $\sigma=\sqrt{10}$.
questions.trick: $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2}{n}}$ — divide given sum by $n$, then root.

questions.q: A data set of 6 values has mean 9. If its standard deviation is 0, then
questions.explanation: SD $=0$ means every deviation from the mean is 0, so every observation must equal the mean, 9.
questions.trick: SD $=0$ forces every observation to equal the mean exactly.

questions.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 6. After removing one number, the mean of the remaining 4 numbers becomes 5. The removed number is
questions.explanation: Sum of 5 numbers $=30$; sum of remaining 4 $=20$; removed number $=30-20=10$.
questions.trick: Removed value = (sum before) − (sum after); use $n\times\text{mean}$ for each sum.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The mean deviation about the mean of a data set is
options: always greater than its standard deviation
always less than or equal to its standard deviation
always equal to its standard deviation
questions.explanation: It is a standard result that mean deviation about the mean never exceeds the standard deviation of the same data.
questions.trick: Standard result: mean deviation about the mean $\le$ standard deviation, always.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For ungrouped data $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with mean $\bar x$, the variance is defined as
questions.explanation: Variance is the mean of the squared deviations from the mean: $\sigma^2=\dfrac1n\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2$.
questions.trick: Variance is mean of squared deviations: $\dfrac1n\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which measure of dispersion is based only on the two extreme observations of a data set?
questions.explanation: Range $=$ maximum value $-$ minimum value, using only the two extreme observations, unlike MD/variance/SD which use every observation.
questions.trick: Range uses only max and min — ignores every other observation.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. The probability that at least one die shows a 6 is
questions.explanation: $P(\text{no 6 on either die})=\left(\dfrac56\right)^2=\dfrac{25}{36}$, so $P(\text{at least one 6})=1-\dfrac{25}{36}=\dfrac{11}{36}$.
questions.trick: 'At least one 6' = 1 − P(neither die shows 6) = $1-(5/6)^2$.

questions.q: If $P(A)=0.35$, then $P(A')$ equals
questions.trick: $P(A')=1-P(A)$ — instant complement.

questions.q: If $P(A)=0.6$, $P(B)=0.5$ and $P(A\cap B)=0.3$, are $A$ and $B$ mutually exclusive?
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events must have $P(A\cap B)=0$; here it is 0.3, so they are not mutually exclusive.
questions.trick: Mutually exclusive requires $P(A\cap B)=0$ — check the given value.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A coin is tossed 4 times. The probability of getting exactly 3 heads is
questions.explanation: Number of ways to choose 3 heads out of 4 tosses is $\binom43=4$; total outcomes $=16$, so $P=4/16=1/4$.

questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive with $P(A)=0.4$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.7$, then $P(B)$ equals
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events, $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B) \Rightarrow 0.7=0.4+P(B) \Rightarrow P(B)=0.3$.
questions.trick: Mutually exclusive: $P(B)=P(A\cup B)-P(A)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The odds in favour of an event are $5:2$. The probability that the event does NOT occur is
questions.explanation: $P(\text{event})=\dfrac{5}{5+2}=\dfrac57$, so $P(\text{not event})=1-\dfrac57=\dfrac27$.
questions.trick: Find $P(\text{event})=a/(a+b)$ from odds, then complement for 'not'.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Let $f:\{1,2,3\}\to\{1,2,3\}$ be defined by $f(1)=2,\ f(2)=3,\ f(3)=1$. Then $f^{-1}$ is given by
questions.explanation: $f$ is a bijection (a 3-cycle), so it is invertible. Since $f(1)=2$, $f^{-1}(2)=1$; since $f(2)=3$, $f^{-1}(3)=2$; since $f(3)=1$, $f^{-1}(1)=3$.

questions.subject: maths

questions.q: On $\mathbb{Q}$, the operation $a*b=\dfrac{ab}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: $a*b=ab/2=ba/2=b*a$ (commutative). $(a*b)*c=(ab/2)*c=abc/4$ and $a*(b*c)=a*(bc/2)=abc/4$, equal (associative).
questions.trick: Check $a*b=b*a$ for commutative, expand both groupings for associative.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $f(x)=x^2+1$ and $g(x)=x-1$, then $(fog)(3)$ equals
questions.trick: Innermost first: find $g(3)$, then apply $f$ to that result.

questions.q: The function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ given by $f(x)=x^2$ is
questions.explanation: $f(-2)=f(2)=4$ so not one-one; negative numbers have no pre-image (since $x^2\ge 0$), so not onto.

questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^3$. Then $f$ is
questions.explanation: $x^3$ is strictly increasing so it is one-one, and as $x$ ranges over $\mathbb{R}$, $x^3$ takes every real value, so it is onto.
questions.trick: Odd-power monomials $x^{2k+1}$ are always bijections on $\mathbb{R}$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Every one-one function from a finite set to itself is onto
Composition of two one-one functions is one-one
Every onto function from a finite set to itself is one-one but need not be invertible
Composition of two onto functions is onto
questions.explanation: On a finite set, an onto function to itself is automatically one-one and hence bijective, so it IS invertible — making option C (which claims it need not be invertible) the false statement.
questions.trick: On a finite set: one-one $\iff$ onto $\iff$ bijective $\iff$ invertible.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of equivalence relations on the set $\{1,2,3\}$ containing $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ is
questions.explanation: Since $1$ and $2$ must be in the same class, the partitions are $\{1,2,3\}$ (all together) or $\{1,2\},\{3\}$ — exactly 2 equivalence relations.
questions.trick: Fixing $1\sim2$ leaves only two possible partitions of the set.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Assertion (A): The identity relation on a set $A$ is always an equivalence relation. Reason (R): The identity relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The identity relation $\{(a,a):a\in A\}$ trivially satisfies all three properties, so both A and R are true and R correctly explains A.
questions.trick: Identity relation $\{(a,a)\}$ trivially satisfies R, S, T — always equivalence.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\sin x$ restricted to $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ with codomain $[-1,1]$. Then $f$ is
questions.explanation: On $\left[-\pi/2,\pi/2\right]$, $\sin x$ is strictly increasing (one-one) and its range is exactly $[-1,1]$ (onto), so it is a bijection — this is the basis for defining $\sin^{-1}x$.
questions.trick: $\sin x$ on $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ is strictly increasing with range $[-1,1]$ — a bijection.

questions.q: If $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}$, then $f$ is

questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The relation $R$ on $\mathbb{N}$ defined by $aRb$ if $a$ divides $b$ is
options: reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
questions.explanation: Every $a$ divides itself (reflexive); if $a|b$ and $b|c$ then $a|c$ (transitive); but $2|4$ does not mean $4|2$, so not symmetric.
questions.trick: 'Divides' is reflexive and transitive, but $2|4$ does not give $4|2$.

questions.q: If $n(A)=3$, the total number of binary operations that can be defined on $A$ is
questions.explanation: A binary operation is a function from $A\times A$ (9 elements) to $A$ (3 choices each), giving $3^9$ possible binary operations.
questions.trick: Binary operations on a set of size $n$: total $n^{n^2}$ (functions $A\times A\to A$).

questions.q: If $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$ are both bijections, then $(gof)^{-1}$ equals
questions.explanation: Standard result: the inverse of a composition reverses the order, $(gof)^{-1}=f^{-1}og^{-1}$.
questions.trick: Inverse of a composite reverses order: $(gof)^{-1}=f^{-1}og^{-1}$.

questions.q: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=3x-5$. Then $f$ is
questions.explanation: $f$ is linear with nonzero slope so it is injective; for any $y\in\mathbb{R}$, $x=(y+5)/3$ gives $f(x)=y$, so it is surjective too.

questions.explanation: Since $\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the sum equals $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and $\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}=0$.

questions.q: The value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}-\sin^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin^{-1}(-1/2)=-\pi/6$, so expression $=\sin(\pi/3+\pi/6)=\sin(\pi/2)=1$.

questions.q: Assertion (A): $\sin^{-1}(\sin 4)$ is not equal to $4$. Reason (R): $4$ radians does not lie in $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Choose the correct option.

A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.q: The domain of $\sin^{-1}(2x-1)$ is
questions.explanation: We need $-1\le 2x-1\le 1 \Rightarrow 0\le 2x\le 2 \Rightarrow 0\le x\le 1$, so the domain is $[0,1]$.

questions.q: $\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x$ equals
questions.explanation: This is a standard identity valid for all $x\in[-1,1]$.

questions.explanation: $3\pi/4$ is outside $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$. $\sin(3\pi/4)=\sin(\pi/4)$, and $\pi/4$ lies in the principal range, so the answer is $\pi/4$.
questions.trick: Use $\sin(\pi-x)=\sin x$ to pull the angle into $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ first.

questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x-1}{x-2}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x+1}{x+2}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then $x$ equals

questions.q: Which of the following is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: $\cos^{-1}$ is not an odd function; the correct identity is $\cos^{-1}(-x)=\pi-\cos^{-1}x$, so option D is false.

Then $\tan^{-1}\frac34+\tan^{-1}\frac17=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac34+\frac17}{1-\frac34\cdot\frac17}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{25}{28}}{\frac{25}{28}}=\tan^{-1}(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.trick: Combine the first pair with the double-angle formula, then add the last term.

questions.explanation: $A^2 = \begin{pmatrix}0\cdot0+1\cdot0 & 0\cdot1+1\cdot0\\ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix} = 0$. $A$ is nilpotent.

questions.q: If $A$ is a square matrix such that $A^2=I$, then $A$ is called
questions.explanation: A matrix satisfying $A^2=I$ (i.e. $A$ is its own inverse) is called involutory.

questions.explanation: For any square matrix $A$, $(A+A')'=A'+A=A+A'$, so $A+A'$ is always symmetric.

questions.trick: $|A^{-1}|=1/|A|$ — reciprocal, no matrix computation needed.

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE for matrix multiplication of square matrices $A,B$ of the same order?
questions.explanation: Since matrix multiplication is not commutative in general, $(A+B)^2=A^2+AB+BA+B^2$ is always true, but it simplifies to $A^2+2AB+B^2$ only when $AB=BA$. The other statements can fail.

questions.q: If $A$ is a non-singular square matrix of order $n$, then $|\text{adj}\,A|$ equals
questions.explanation: The standard identity is $|\text{adj}\,A|=|A|^{n-1}$ for an $n\times n$ matrix.
questions.trick: Memorize $|\text{adj}\,A|=|A|^{n-1}$ — a standard one-liner result.

questions.q: The number of possible matrices of order $3\times2$ with each entry either 1 or 2 is
questions.explanation: There are $3\times2=6$ entries, each with 2 choices (1 or 2), giving $2^6=64$ matrices.
questions.trick: $k$ choices per entry over $m\times n$ entries gives $k^{mn}$ matrices.

questions.q: If $A = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 2\\ 3 & 4\end{pmatrix}$, then $A^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: $|A| = 4 - 6 = -2$. $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-2}\begin{pmatrix}4 & -2\\ -3 & 1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}-2 & 1\\ 3/2 & -1/2\end{pmatrix}$.
questions.trick: $A^{-1}=\dfrac1{|A|}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$ — swap diagonal, negate off-diagonal.

questions.q: Every square matrix $A$ can be expressed as
options: sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix
difference of two symmetric matrices only

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of the same order, then $AB-BA$ is always
questions.explanation: $(AB-BA)'=B'A'-A'B'=BA-AB=-(AB-BA)$, so $AB-BA$ is skew-symmetric.
questions.trick: For symmetric $A,B$: $AB-BA$ is always skew-symmetric (transpose flips its sign).

questions.q: If $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, then $A+2B$ equals
questions.explanation: $2B=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\0&-2\end{pmatrix}$, so $A+2B=\begin{pmatrix}2+2&-1+4\\3+0&4-2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4&3\\3&2\end{pmatrix}$.
questions.trick: Scale then add entrywise — no shortcut, just careful entry-by-entry arithmetic.

questions.q: If $A$ is a $3\times3$ matrix with $|A|=3$, then $|A\cdot\text{adj}\,A|$ equals
questions.explanation: $A\cdot\text{adj}\,A=|A|I$, so $|A\cdot\text{adj}\,A|=|A|^3=|A|^n=3^3=27$ for $n=3$.
questions.trick: $|A\cdot\text{adj}\,A|=|A|^n$ since $A\cdot\text{adj}\,A=|A|I$.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\-2&0\end{pmatrix}$ is skew-symmetric. Reason (R): For a skew-symmetric matrix, $A'=-A$.

A is true, R is false
