questions.q: If $A$ is a $3\times3$ matrix and $k$ is a scalar, then $|kA|$ equals
questions.explanation: For an $n\times n$ matrix, $|kA|=k^n|A|$; here $n=3$, so $|kA|=k^3|A|$.
questions.trick: $|kA|=k^n|A|$ — same rule, $n=3$ here too.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For what value of $k$ are the points $(k,2)$, $(2,4)$ and $(3,2)$ collinear?
questions.explanation: Collinear $\Rightarrow \begin{vmatrix}k&2&1\\2&4&1\\3&2&1\end{vmatrix}=0$. Expanding: $k(4-2)-2(2-3)+1(4-12)=2k+2-8=2k-6=0\Rightarrow k=3$.
questions.trick: Set the area (collinearity) determinant to $0$ and solve the linear equation.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}a&b&c\\p&q&r\\x&y&z\end{vmatrix}=10$, then the value of $\begin{vmatrix}p&q&r\\a&b&c\\x&y&z\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: Interchanging any two rows of a determinant changes its sign, so the new determinant is $-10$.
questions.trick: Swapping any two rows just flips the sign of the determinant.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $\begin{vmatrix}0&a&-b\\-a&0&c\\b&-c&0\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: This is a skew-symmetric determinant of odd order (3); such determinants always equal $0$.
questions.trick: Skew-symmetric odd-order determinant is always $0$ — no computation needed.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For a homogeneous system of 3 linear equations in 3 unknowns, a non-trivial (non-zero) solution exists if and only if the determinant of the coefficient matrix is
questions.explanation: A homogeneous system $AX=0$ has a non-trivial solution exactly when $A$ is singular, i.e. $|A|=0$; otherwise $A^{-1}$ exists and the only solution is the trivial one $X=0$.
questions.trick: Non-trivial solution to $AX=0$ exists iff $|A|=0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A$ is a skew-symmetric matrix of odd order, then $|A|$ equals
questions.explanation: For a skew-symmetric matrix of odd order $n$, $|A|=|A^T|=|-A|=(-1)^n|A|=-|A|$, forcing $|A|=0$.
questions.trick: Skew-symmetric determinant of ODD order always equals $0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The cofactor of the element $6$ in the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&3\\4&5&6\\7&8&9\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.trick: Cofactor $=(-1)^{i+j}\times$minor — watch the sign flip.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The determinant $\begin{vmatrix}102&18&36\\1&3&4\\17&3&6\end{vmatrix}$ can be simplified by first taking out a common factor of
questions.explanation: Row 1 entries $102,18,36$ are all divisible by $6$ ($=17\times6,3\times6,6\times6$), so $6$ can be factored out of row 1 to simplify the calculation.
questions.trick: Spot the GCD of a row's entries and factor it out before expanding.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If two rows of a $3\times3$ determinant are identical, the value of the determinant is
questions.explanation: A determinant with two identical rows (or columns) is always equal to $0$.
questions.trick: Two identical rows or columns $\Rightarrow$ determinant is $0$ instantly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A$ is a $2\times2$ matrix with $|A|=3$, then $|A^{-1}|$ equals
questions.trick: $|A^{-1}|$ is simply the reciprocal of $|A|$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(4,0)$ and $(0,3)$ is
questions.explanation: Right triangle with legs 4 and 3: Area $=\dfrac12\times4\times3=6$.
questions.trick: Right-triangle area $=\tfrac12\times$base$\times$height, no determinant needed.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The points $(1,2)$, $(2,4)$ and $(3,6)$ are
options: vertices of a triangle with area 1
questions.explanation: $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&1\\2&4&1\\3&6&1\end{vmatrix}=1(4-6)-2(2-3)+1(12-12)=-2+2+0=0$, so the area is zero and the points are collinear.
questions.trick: Area-determinant $=0$ $\Rightarrow$ the three points are collinear.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The determinant $\begin{vmatrix}1&\cos\theta&1\\-\cos\theta&1&\cos\theta\\-1&-\cos\theta&1\end{vmatrix}$ lies in the range
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row gives the value $2+2\cos^2\theta$, which lies between $2$ and $4$ as $\cos^2\theta\in[0,1]$.
questions.trick: Expand along a row, then bound the resulting $\cos^2\theta$ term between $0$ and $1$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For the system $3x+2y=5$, $6x+4y=k$ to have infinitely many solutions, $k$ must equal
questions.explanation: The second equation is a multiple of the first: $6x+4y=2(3x+2y)$. For infinitely many solutions the RHS must scale the same way: $k=2\times5=10$.
questions.trick: Proportional coefficients $\Rightarrow$ RHS must scale by the same factor as the rows.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\begin{vmatrix}x&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}=8$, then $x$ equals
questions.explanation: $x^2-1=8\Rightarrow x^2=9\Rightarrow x=\pm3$.
questions.trick: Solve $x^2-1=8$ like a quick quadratic, take the $\pm$ root.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A$ is an invertible matrix and $A^T=A^{-1}$, then $A$ is called
questions.explanation: By definition, a square matrix satisfying $A^TA=AA^T=I$ (i.e. $A^T=A^{-1}$) is called an orthogonal matrix.
questions.trick: $A^T=A^{-1}$ defines an orthogonal matrix.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If one row of a $3\times3$ matrix $A$ is multiplied by a scalar $5$ to get matrix $B$, then $|B|$ equals
questions.explanation: Multiplying a single row by a scalar $k$ multiplies the determinant by $k$ (not $k^n$), so $|B|=5|A|$.
questions.trick: Scaling ONE row by $k$ multiplies the determinant by $k$ (not $k^n$).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The value of $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&4\\0&0&1\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: For an upper triangular matrix, the determinant equals the product of diagonal entries: $1\times1\times1=1$.
questions.trick: Triangular/diagonal matrix: determinant $=$ product of diagonal entries.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The system of equations $2x+3y=5$, $4x+6y=10$ has
questions.explanation: The determinant $\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\4&6\end{vmatrix}=12-12=0$, and the second equation is exactly twice the first, so the equations are consistent with infinitely many solutions.
questions.trick: $\Delta=0$ and one equation is a multiple of the other $\Rightarrow$ infinite solutions.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The derivative of $\sin x$ with respect to $\log x$ is
questions.explanation: Let $u=\log x$. Then $\dfrac{d(\sin x)}{du}=\dfrac{d(\sin x)/dx}{du/dx}=\dfrac{\cos x}{1/x}=x\cos x$.
questions.trick: Derivative of $f$ w.r.t. $g$ equals $f'(x)/g'(x)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $x^2+y^2=1$, then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at the point $(0,1)$ equals
questions.explanation: Differentiating: $2x+2yy'=0\Rightarrow y'=-x/y$. At $(0,1)$, $y'=0$. Differentiating again, $y''=-\dfrac{y-xy'}{y^2}$; at $(0,1)$, $y''=-\dfrac{1-0}{1}=-1$.
questions.trick: Differentiate implicitly twice; substitute the point only at the end.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The derivative of $\log_{10}x$ with respect to $x$ is
questions.explanation: $\log_{10}x=\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln10}$, so its derivative is $\dfrac{1}{x\ln10}$.
questions.trick: Convert $\log_a x$ to $\ln x/\ln a$ before differentiating.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: By the Mean Value Theorem, for $f(x)=x^2$ on $[1,4]$, the value of $c$ is
questions.trick: MVT: set $f'(c)$ equal to the average slope $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$, solve.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $x=at^2$ and $y=2at$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: $dx/dt=2at$, $dy/dt=2a$. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2a}{2at}=\dfrac{1}{t}$.
questions.trick: Parametric: divide $dy/dt$ by $dx/dt$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The function $f(x)=\begin{cases}x, & x<1\\5, & x=1\\2x+1,&x>1\end{cases}$ is
options: discontinuous at $x=1$ since left limit does not equal right limit
discontinuous at $x=1$ since left and right limits differ from $f(1)$
questions.explanation: Left limit $=1$, right limit $=2(1)+1=3$; since these two limits are unequal, $f$ is discontinuous at $x=1$ (regardless of $f(1)=5$).
questions.trick: Left limit $\ne$ right limit alone is enough to prove discontinuity.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $x=a\cos^3\theta$ and $y=a\sin^3\theta$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=-3a\cos^2\theta\sin\theta$, $\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta$. Dividing gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=-\tan\theta$.
questions.trick: Astroid-type parametric curve: $dy/dx=-\tan\theta$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $x^2+y^2=25$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at the point $(3,4)$ is
questions.explanation: Differentiating implicitly: $2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-x/y=-3/4$.
questions.trick: Implicit differentiation on a circle gives $dy/dx=-x/y$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}3x-2,&x<2\\2k,&x=2\\x+2,&x>2\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=2$, then $k$ equals
questions.explanation: Left limit $=3(2)-2=4$, right limit $=2+2=4$. For continuity, $f(2)=2k$ must equal this common limit: $2k=4\Rightarrow k=2$.
questions.trick: Match left limit $=$ right limit $=f(a)$, then solve for the unknown.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=e^{x}\cos x$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: By the product rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^x\cos x+e^x(-\sin x)=e^x(\cos x-\sin x)$.
questions.trick: Product rule: $(uv)'=u'v+uv'$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\cos^{-1}x\right)$ equals
questions.explanation: Standard derivative formula: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\cos^{-1}x=\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, opposite in sign to $\sin^{-1}x$'s derivative.
questions.trick: $\sin^{-1}x$ and $\cos^{-1}x$ have equal-magnitude, opposite-sign derivatives.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For $f(x)=\ln x$ on $[1,e]$, the value of $c$ guaranteed by the Mean Value Theorem is
questions.explanation: $f'(c)=\dfrac{f(e)-f(1)}{e-1}=\dfrac{1-0}{e-1}=\dfrac{1}{e-1}$. Since $f'(x)=1/x$, $1/c=1/(e-1)\Rightarrow c=e-1$.
questions.trick: MVT slope for $\ln x$ over $[1,e]$ is $1/(e-1)$; solve $f'(c)=$ that.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=\sin^{-1}(3x-4x^3)$ for $|x|\le1/2$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: For $|x|\le1/2$, $\sin^{-1}(3x-4x^3)=3\sin^{-1}x$ (triple-angle identity), so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
questions.trick: Spot the disguised triple-angle: $\sin^{-1}(3x-4x^3)=3\sin^{-1}x$ for $|x|\le\tfrac12$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ for $|x|\le1$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: For $|x|\le1$, $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$.
questions.trick: Spot the disguised double-angle: $\sin^{-1}\left(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$ for $|x|\le1$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is an even function (i.e. $f(-x)=f(x)$) and is differentiable, then $f'(x)$ is
options: neither even nor odd in general
questions.explanation: Differentiating $f(-x)=f(x)$ using the chain rule gives $-f'(-x)=f'(x)$, i.e. $f'(-x)=-f'(x)$ — the definition of an odd function.
questions.trick: Differentiate the even-function identity $f(-x)=f(x)$ to see the sign flip.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $f(x)=x|x|$, then at $x=0$, $f(x)$ is
questions.explanation: For $x\ge0$, $f(x)=x^2$; for $x<0$, $f(x)=-x^2$. Both left and right derivatives at $0$ equal $0$, so $f$ is differentiable there with $f'(0)=0$.
questions.trick: Split into cases ($x\ge0$, $x<0$) and check that left/right derivatives match.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=\log(\log x)$ for $x>1$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{\log x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}=\dfrac{1}{x\log x}$.
questions.trick: Chain rule twice: outer log, then inner log, multiply the two factors.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $x=a\cos\theta$, $y=a\sin\theta$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=-a\sin\theta$, $\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=a\cos\theta$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{a\cos\theta}{-a\sin\theta}=-\cot\theta$.
questions.trick: Parametric circle: $dy/dx=-\cot\theta$, the ratio of the $\theta$-derivatives.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A function $f$ satisfies $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y$, with $f(0)\ne0$. If $f(3)=2$ and $f'(0)=4$, then $f'(3)$ equals
questions.explanation: Differentiating $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ with respect to $y$ and setting $y=0$ gives $f'(x)=f(x)f'(0)$. So $f'(3)=f(3)\cdot f'(0)=2\times4=8$.
questions.trick: For $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$, always $f'(x)=f(x)f'(0)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{\sin x}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: $y=(\sin x)^{1/2}$; by chain rule $y'=\dfrac12(\sin x)^{-1/2}\cos x=\dfrac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}$.
questions.trick: Write as $(\sin x)^{1/2}$ and apply the chain rule with the power rule.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=(\sin x)^x$ for $0<x<\pi$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: Take $\ln$: $\ln y=x\ln(\sin x)$. Differentiating, $y'/y=\ln(\sin x)+x\cdot\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}=\ln(\sin x)+x\cot x$, so $y'=(\sin x)^x[\ln(\sin x)+x\cot x]$.
questions.trick: Variable base and exponent: take log first, then use the product rule.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)$ for $|x|<1$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equals
questions.explanation: Using the substitution $x=\tan\phi$, $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}=2\tan^{-1}x$, so $y=2\tan^{-1}x$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$.
questions.trick: Spot the disguised double-angle: $\tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$ for $|x|<1$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $f(a)=f(b)$, this is the hypothesis of
questions.explanation: These are exactly the conditions of Rolle's Theorem, which concludes that some $c\in(a,b)$ has $f'(c)=0$.
questions.trick: $f(a)=f(b)$ plus continuity/differentiability is exactly Rolle's setup.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y=x^3-3x^2+2$, then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $x=1$ equals
questions.trick: Differentiate twice, then just substitute the given $x$ value.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Using differentials, the approximate value of $\sqrt{25.2}$ is
questions.trick: $\Delta y\approx f'(x)\Delta x$ — pick the nearest perfect square/cube as the base point.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A cylindrical tank's volume is increasing at $50\,\text{cm}^3/\text{s}$ while its radius stays fixed at $r=5\,\text{cm}$. The rate at which the height is increasing is
questions.explanation: $V=\pi r^2h\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\pi r^2\dfrac{dh}{dt}$ (r fixed). $50=\pi(25)\dfrac{dh}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{50}{25\pi}=\dfrac{2}{\pi}$.
questions.trick: Fixed radius $\Rightarrow dV/dt=\pi r^2\,dh/dt$, solve for $dh/dt$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The absolute maximum value of $f(x)=x^2$ on $[-2,3]$ is
questions.explanation: Compare endpoints and critical point $x=0$: $f(-2)=4$, $f(3)=9$, $f(0)=0$. Maximum is $9$ at $x=3$.
questions.trick: Absolute max/min: compare $f$ at critical points AND both endpoints.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The rate of change of the area of a circle with respect to its radius $r$ when $r=5\,\text{cm}$ is
questions.explanation: $A=\pi r^2\Rightarrow \dfrac{dA}{dr}=2\pi r=2\pi(5)=10\pi$.
questions.trick: $dA/dr=2\pi r$ — just plug in $r$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two positive numbers whose sum is 16 and whose product is maximum are
questions.explanation: Let numbers be $x,16-x$; product $P=16x-x^2$, $P'=16-2x=0\Rightarrow x=8$. Numbers are 8 and 8.
questions.trick: Fixed sum $\Rightarrow$ product is maximized when the two numbers are equal.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x+\dfrac{1}{x}$ (for $x>0$) has a local minimum at
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}=0\Rightarrow x^2=1\Rightarrow x=1$ (taking $x>0$). Since $f''(x)=\dfrac{2}{x^3}>0$ at $x=1$, it is a local minimum.
questions.trick: Classic $x+1/x$ has its minimum at $x=1$ for $x>0$ (AM-GM intuition).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The maximum value of $f(x)=-x^2+4x+1$ is
questions.trick: Downward parabola: vertex is the max — set $f'(x)=0$, confirm $f''<0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A kite is flying at a constant height of 90 m and moves horizontally away from the flyer at $5\,\text{m/s}$. When the kite is 120 m horizontally away (so the string is 150 m long), the rate at which the string is being let out is
questions.explanation: Let $x$ = horizontal distance, height $=90$ (constant), string $l$: $l^2=x^2+90^2$. Here $x=120,\ l=150$ (since $90^2+120^2=150^2$). Differentiating: $2l\dfrac{dl}{dt}=2x\dfrac{dx}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dl}{dt}=\dfrac{x}{l}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{120}{150}\times5=4\,\text{m/s}$.
questions.trick: Right-triangle relation $l^2=x^2+h^2$; differentiate, then plug in known values.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x^2-4x+7$ is strictly increasing on
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=2x-4>0\Rightarrow x>2$.
questions.trick: $f'(x)>0$ gives the increasing interval — solve the linear inequality.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The local minimum value of $f(x)=x^3-3x+2$ is
questions.trick: Solve $f'(x)=0$, then use the sign of $f''$ to pick the minimum root.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The absolute minimum value of $f(x)=x^2-2x+3$ on $[0,3]$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=2x-2=0\Rightarrow x=1$ (in $[0,3]$), $f(1)=1-2+3=2$. Compare with endpoints: $f(0)=3$, $f(3)=9-6+3=6$. The minimum among these is $2$.
questions.trick: Check the critical point AND both endpoints, then pick the smallest value.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin x+\cos x$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt2\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, whose maximum value is $\sqrt2$.
questions.trick: $a\sin x+b\cos x$ has max value $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ — here $\sqrt2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A wire of length 28 m is cut into two pieces; one is bent into a square and the other into a circle. For the combined area of the square and circle to be minimum, the length of wire used for the square is
questions.explanation: Let $x$ = wire for the square (side $x/4$, area $x^2/16$); remaining $(28-x)$ forms the circle ($r=(28-x)/(2\pi)$, area $(28-x)^2/(4\pi)$). Minimising $A(x)=\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{(28-x)^2}{4\pi}$: $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{x}{8}-\dfrac{28-x}{2\pi}=0\Rightarrow 2\pi x=8(28-x)\Rightarrow x(2\pi+8)=224\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{224}{2\pi+8}=\dfrac{112}{\pi+4}$.
questions.trick: Express total area as a function of one cut length, differentiate, set to $0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Using differentials, the approximate value of $(8.01)^{1/3}$ is
questions.trick: Linear approximation $f(x+dx)\approx f(x)+f'(x)dx$ with $x$ a nearby perfect cube.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If the side of a square is increasing at $3\,\text{cm/s}$, the rate at which its area is increasing when the side is $10\,\text{cm}$ is
questions.explanation: $A=s^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dt}=2s\dfrac{ds}{dt}=2(10)(3)=60\,\text{cm}^2/\text{s}$.
questions.trick: $dA/dt=2s\cdot ds/dt$ for a square — chain rule on $A=s^2$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{(x+1)(x^2+1)}=\dfrac12\ln|x+1|+p\ln(x^2+1)+q\tan^{-1}x+C$, then $p+q$ equals
questions.explanation: Partial fractions give $\dfrac1{(x+1)(x^2+1)}=\dfrac{1/2}{x+1}+\dfrac{-x/2+1/2}{x^2+1}$, so $p=-\dfrac14$ and $q=\dfrac12$; thus $p+q=\dfrac14$.
questions.trick: Match coefficients after partial fractions with an irreducible quadratic factor.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \frac{2x}{x^2+1}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: With $t=x^2+1,\ dt=2x\,dx$: $\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=\ln|t|+C=\ln(x^2+1)+C$.
questions.trick: Numerator is exactly the derivative of the denominator $\Rightarrow$ answer is $\ln|\text{denominator}|$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int_2^9 f(x)\,dx=11$, then $\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{4} f(x+5)\,dx$ equals
questions.explanation: Substitute $u=x+5$; the limits become $u=2$ and $u=9$, matching the given integral exactly, so the value is unchanged at $11$.
questions.trick: A shift $x\to x+c$ inside $f$ just shifts the limits by $c$ — value unchanged.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \frac{x}{1 + x^2}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\tfrac12\int_0^1\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}dx = \tfrac12[\ln(1+x^2)]_0^1 = \tfrac12\ln2$.
questions.trick: Substitute $t=1+x^2$; the numerator matches $dt/2$ exactly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x} + \sqrt{\cos x}}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Let $I$ be the integral. By $\int_0^a f(x)dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)dx$, $I = \int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\cos x}+\sqrt{\sin x}}dx$. Adding, $2I = \pi/2$.
questions.trick: Add $I$ to its $(a-x)$-mirror to cancel the messy roots — King's rule classic.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2} x^3\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $x^3$ is an odd function and the interval $[-2,2]$ is symmetric about $0$, so the definite integral is $0$.
questions.trick: $x^3$ is odd $\Rightarrow$ integral over $[-a,a]$ is $0$ instantly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} x\sin x\cos x\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Write $x\sin x\cos x=\tfrac{x}{2}\sin2x$; integrating by parts with $u=x/2,\,dv=\sin2x\,dx$ gives $\left[-\tfrac{x}{4}\cos2x+\tfrac18\sin2x\right]_0^{\pi/2}=\tfrac{\pi}{8}$.
questions.trick: Convert $\sin x\cos x$ to $\tfrac12\sin2x$ first, then integrate by parts.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_1^5 \dfrac{5^{\sqrt{x-1}}}{5^{\sqrt{x-1}}+5^{\sqrt{5-x}}}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: With $I$ the given integral, substituting $x\to6-x$ swaps the two exponents, giving the complementary fraction; adding, $2I=\int_1^5 1\,dx=4$, so $I=2$.
questions.trick: Numerator + swapped-numerator = denominator ⇒ sum of $I$ and its mirror is just the interval length.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \frac{x}{x^2+1}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Let $t=x^2+1,\ dt=2x\,dx$: $\int\dfrac{x\,dx}{x^2+1}=\dfrac12\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=\dfrac12\ln(x^2+1)+C$.
questions.trick: Numerator is half the derivative of the denominator $\Rightarrow$ answer is $\tfrac12\ln|\text{denominator}|$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int x\ln x\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: By parts with $u=\ln x, dv=x\,dx$: $\int x\ln x\,dx=\dfrac{x^2}2\ln x-\int\dfrac{x^2}2\cdot\dfrac1x\,dx=\dfrac{x^2}2\ln x-\dfrac{x^2}4+C$.
questions.trick: By parts with $u=\ln x,\,dv=x\,dx$ — a standard combo, memorize the result form.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \frac{dx}{x^2+2x+5}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $x^2+2x+5=(x+1)^2+4$. Using $\int\dfrac{dx}{u^2+a^2}=\dfrac1a\tan^{-1}\dfrac ua+C$ with $u=x+1,a=2$: $\dfrac12\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+1}{2}\right)+C$.
questions.trick: Complete the square first, then apply the standard $\tan^{-1}$ form.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int e^x(\sin x + \cos x)\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Of the form $\int e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]dx$ with $f = \sin x$, $f' = \cos x$ → $e^x\sin x$.
questions.trick: Spot the $e^x[f(x)+f'(x)]$ form $\Rightarrow$ answer is $e^xf(x)$ directly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\sin^7x\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\sin^7x$ is an odd function, so the integral over $[-a, a]$ is zero.
questions.trick: Odd power of $\sin$/$\cos$ over symmetric limits $\to$ integral is $0$ instantly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer not greater than $x$, then $\displaystyle\int_0^3 [x]\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $[x]=0,1,2$ on the intervals $[0,1),[1,2),[2,3)$ respectively, each of length $1$, so the integral is $0+1+2=3$.
questions.trick: Split at each integer; $[x]$ is constant on every unit interval.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\int_0^\pi\sin x\,dx=[-\cos x]_0^\pi=-\cos\pi-(-\cos0)=1+1=2$.
questions.trick: $\int\sin x=-\cos x$; evaluating at $\pi$ and $0$ gives $2$ (it's not odd about $\pi$).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \frac{dx}{x^2-4}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using $\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2-a^2}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\dfrac{x-a}{x+a}\right|+C$ with $a=2$: $\dfrac14\ln\left|\dfrac{x-2}{x+2}\right|+C$.
questions.trick: $\int dx/(x^2-a^2)$ standard log form — plug $a=2$, keep the $1/(2a)$ factor.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x\left[2(\ln x)^2+3\ln x+1\right]}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Put $t=\ln x$, $dt=dx/x$; factor $2t^2+3t+1=(2t+1)(t+1)$ and use partial fractions $\dfrac{1}{(2t+1)(t+1)}=\dfrac{2}{2t+1}-\dfrac1{t+1}$ to get $\ln|2t+1|-\ln|t+1|+C$.
questions.trick: Substitute $t=\ln x$ to turn a log-quadratic denominator into a factorable partial-fraction problem.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int x^2\,e^{x^3}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Let $t=x^3$, $dt=3x^2dx$. Then $\int x^2e^{x^3}dx=\dfrac13\int e^t dt=\dfrac13e^{x^3}+C$.
questions.trick: Substitute $t=x^3$; $dt=3x^2dx$ matches the $x^2$ term exactly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \frac{dx}{x\ln x}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Put $t = \ln x$, $dt = dx/x$: $\int dt/t = \ln|t|$.
questions.trick: Substitute $t=\ln x$, reduces to $\int dt/t=\ln|t|$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int e^x(\cot x-\csc^2x)\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: With $f(x)=\cot x$, $f'(x)=-\csc^2x$, so $\cot x-\csc^2x=f(x)+f'(x)$, giving $\int e^x[f+f']dx=e^xf(x)=e^x\cot x+C$.
questions.trick: Spot $\cot x$ and its derivative $-\csc^2x$ together ⇒ instant $e^x\cot x$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\cos x\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $x^3\cos x$ is odd (odd × even), so the integral over a symmetric interval is zero.
questions.trick: Odd function over symmetric limits $\to$ integral is $0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \frac{dx}{x^2 - a^2}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Partial fractions: $\dfrac{1}{x^2-a^2} = \dfrac1{2a}\left(\dfrac1{x-a} - \dfrac1{x+a}\right)$.
questions.trick: Partial fractions: $\dfrac1{x^2-a^2}=\dfrac1{2a}\left(\dfrac1{x-a}-\dfrac1{x+a}\right)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sin^3x}{\cos^5x}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Write $\dfrac{\sin^3x}{\cos^5x}=\tan^3x\sec^2x$; with $t=\tan x$, $dt=\sec^2x\,dx$ gives $\int t^3dt=\dfrac{t^4}{4}=\dfrac{\tan^4x}{4}+C$.
questions.trick: $\sin^m x/\cos^{m+2}x$ always reduces to $\tan^{m+1}x/(m+1)$ via $t=\tan x$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: By property of definite integrals, $\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx=\displaystyle\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$. Using this, $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$ equals
questions.explanation: Let $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$. By the property, $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$ too (replacing $x\to\pi/2-x$ swaps sin and cos). Adding, $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}1\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $I=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.trick: Add $I$ to its sin-cos-swapped twin — the sum becomes $\int1\,dx$, then halve it.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by $y=\sqrt x$ and $y=x$ between $x=0$ and $x=1$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\sqrt x\ge x$ on $[0,1]$, $A=\int_0^1(\sqrt x-x)dx=\left[\dfrac23x^{3/2}-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1=\dfrac23-\dfrac12=\dfrac16$.
questions.trick: Compare $\sqrt x$ and $x$ on $[0,1]$: $\sqrt x$ is always on top.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$ and the coordinate axes is
questions.explanation: Full ellipse area $=\pi ab=\pi(4)(3)=12\pi$; the first-quadrant quarter is $3\pi$.
questions.trick: Quarter-ellipse $=\tfrac14\pi ab$, the same shortcut as for a circle.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by $y=x^2$ and $y=|x|$ for $-1\le x\le1$ is
questions.explanation: Since $|x|\ge x^2$ on $[-1,1]$, $A=2\int_0^1(x-x^2)dx=2\left(\dfrac12-\dfrac13\right)=2\times\dfrac16=\dfrac13$.
questions.trick: By symmetry compute for $x\ge0$ and double: check which curve sits on top.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by $y=x^2-4$ and the x-axis between $x=-2$ and $x=2$ is
questions.explanation: Since $y\le0$ on $[-2,2]$, area $=\left|\int_{-2}^2(x^2-4)dx\right|=\left|\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-4x\right]_{-2}^2\right|=\left|-\dfrac{32}{3}\right|=\dfrac{32}{3}$.
questions.trick: Curve dips below the axis: take $|\int|$, don't report the negative raw value.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by $y=x$, the x-axis and $x=0,x=4$ is
questions.explanation: $A=\int_0^4 x\,dx=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4=8$.
questions.trick: $y=x$ is a line: check $\frac12\times\text{base}\times\text{height}$ against the integral.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by $y=x^2$ and $y=x$ is
questions.explanation: Intersections at $x=0,1$. $A=\int_0^1(x-x^2)\,dx=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\dfrac12-\dfrac13=\dfrac16$.
questions.trick: Between two curves: find intersections first, then $\int(\text{top}-\text{bottom})$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}$ is
questions.explanation: Separating variables, $\dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{dx}{x} \Rightarrow \ln|y| = \ln|x| + \ln C \Rightarrow y = Cx$.
questions.trick: $dy/y=dx/x$ separates instantly; the solution is always $y=Cx$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $y = e^{mx}$ is a solution of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 5\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 6y = 0$, the possible values of $m$ are
questions.explanation: Substituting $y=e^{mx}$ gives $m^2 - 5m + 6 = 0 \Rightarrow (m-2)(m-3)=0 \Rightarrow m=2,3$.
questions.trick: Substitute $y=e^{mx}$: turns the DE into a quadratic in $m$ (auxiliary equation).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The differential equation of the family of parabolas $y^2=4a(x-b)$, where $a,b$ are arbitrary constants, is
questions.explanation: Differentiating once: $2yy'=4a$. Differentiating again (RHS is constant): $2(y')^2+2yy''=0$, i.e. $yy''+(y')^2=0$.
questions.trick: Two constants: differentiate twice to eliminate both, landing on a 2nd-order DE.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The order and degree of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+5\dfrac{dy}{dx}-6y=\log x$ are
questions.explanation: The highest order derivative is $d^2y/dx^2$ (order 2) and it appears to the first power (degree 1); $\log x$ is just a function of $x$, not of a derivative.
questions.trick: A pure function of $x$ (like $\log x$) never affects the degree.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2xy}{1+x^2}$ and $y(0)=1$, then $y(1) =$
questions.explanation: Separating, $\dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}dx \Rightarrow \ln y = \ln(1+x^2)+C \Rightarrow y=A(1+x^2)$. Using $y(0)=1$ gives $A=1$, so $y=1+x^2$; $y(1)=2$.
questions.trick: Numerator is the derivative of the denominator $\Rightarrow$ separates straight to $\ln$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The degree of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \sin\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 0$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\sin(dy/dx)$ is not a polynomial expression in the derivative, the degree of this (order 1) equation is not defined.
questions.trick: Trig or exp of a derivative $\Rightarrow$ degree not defined — spot it instantly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The differential equation of the family of lines $y=mx+c$, where $m$ and $c$ are arbitrary constants, is
questions.explanation: Since there are two arbitrary constants, differentiate twice: $y'=m$ (constant), so $y''=0$.
questions.trick: Two constants $\Rightarrow$ differentiate twice to eliminate both, giving $y''=0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of arbitrary constants present in the particular solution of a differential equation of order 3 is
questions.explanation: A particular solution is obtained by assigning specific values to all arbitrary constants using given conditions, leaving none free.
questions.trick: Particular solution: every constant gets evaluated, so zero remain free.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Which of the following differential equations is homogeneous?
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{x+y}{x-y}$ is a function of $y/x$ alone (degree 0 in $x,y$), so it is homogeneous; the others mix terms of different degrees or have a constant term.
questions.trick: Check: can the RHS be written purely as a function of $y/x$?
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-x}{y}$ represents a family of
questions.explanation: Separating, $y\,dy = -x\,dx \Rightarrow \dfrac{y^2}{2} = -\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C \Rightarrow x^2+y^2 = 2C$, a family of concentric circles.
questions.trick: $y\,dy=-x\,dx$ integrates to a circle $x^2+y^2=\text{const}$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Eliminating the arbitrary constant $r$ from the family of circles $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$ gives the differential equation
questions.explanation: Differentiating $x^2+y^2=r^2$ w.r.t. $x$: $2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow x + y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$.
questions.trick: One constant to eliminate $\Rightarrow$ differentiate implicitly just once.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 + y = 0$ are
questions.explanation: The highest derivative present is $dy/dx$ (order 1), raised to the power 3 (degree 3).
questions.trick: Count the power on the single highest derivative present, for degree.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: An equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to only one independent variable is called
questions.explanation: By definition, a differential equation with derivatives taken with respect to a single independent variable is called ordinary (as opposed to partial).
questions.trick: One independent variable $\Rightarrow$ ordinary; more than one $\Rightarrow$ partial.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$ is called
questions.explanation: By definition, such an equation, expressible as a function of $y/x$ alone, is a homogeneous differential equation.
questions.trick: A function of $y/x$ alone (degree-0 in $x,y$) is homogeneous.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The number of arbitrary constants in the general solution of a differential equation of order 4 is
questions.explanation: A general solution of an $n$th order differential equation contains exactly $n$ independent arbitrary constants.
questions.trick: General solution's constant count always equals the order of the DE.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are nonzero vectors and $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 0$, then $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are
questions.explanation: The dot product vanishes only when $\cos\theta=0$, i.e. $\theta = 90^\circ$, so the vectors are perpendicular.
questions.trick: Zero dot product $\Rightarrow$ perpendicular vectors, since $\cos\theta=0$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The point dividing the line joining $A(2,3,4)$ and $B(4,5,6)$ internally in the ratio $2:1$ is
questions.trick: Internal division ratio $m{:}n$: point $=(m\vec b+n\vec a)/(m+n)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\hat a$ and $\hat b$ are unit vectors with angle $60^\circ$ between them, then $\hat a\cdot\hat b =$
questions.explanation: $\hat a\cdot\hat b = |\hat a||\hat b|\cos60^\circ = 1\times1\times0.5 = 0.5$.
questions.trick: For unit vectors, $\hat a\cdot\hat b=\cos\theta$ directly — no magnitudes needed.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: $(\hat i \times \hat j)\cdot \hat k =$
questions.explanation: $\hat i\times\hat j = \hat k$, so $(\hat i\times\hat j)\cdot\hat k = \hat k\cdot\hat k = 1$.
questions.trick: $\hat i\times\hat j=\hat k$ identity, then $\hat k\cdot\hat k=1$ — memorise the cyclic triad.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The work done by a force $\vec F=2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k$ in producing a displacement $\vec d=\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: Work $=\vec F\cdot\vec d=2-3+2=1$.
questions.trick: Work done by a force $=\vec F\cdot\vec d$ (dot product), never cross product.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=4$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b=6$, then $|\vec a\times\vec b|=$
questions.explanation: $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2=144-36=108$, so $|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{108}=6\sqrt3$.
questions.trick: $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2$ links dot and cross.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The projection of $\vec a = \hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ on $\vec b = 2\hat i-2\hat j+\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 2-2+1 = 1$, $|\vec b| = \sqrt{4+4+1}=3$, so the projection $= \dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|} = \dfrac13$.
questions.trick: Projection of $\vec a$ on $\vec b$ is $(\vec a\cdot\vec b)/|\vec b|$, divide by $|\vec b|$ only.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\vec a = 2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b = \hat i+\hat j-2\hat k$, then $\vec a+\vec b =$
questions.explanation: Adding components: $(2+1)\hat i+(-1+1)\hat j+(1-2)\hat k = 3\hat i - \hat k$.
questions.trick: Add or subtract vectors component-wise: $\hat i,\hat j,\hat k$ terms separately.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The direction ratios of $\vec{AB}$, where $A(1,0,0)$ and $B(0,1,1)$, are
questions.trick: DRs of $\vec{AB}=B-A$, component-wise subtraction, no need to normalise.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The magnitude of $\vec a = 2\hat i - 3\hat j + 6\hat k$ is
questions.trick: $|\vec a|=\sqrt{\text{sum of squares of components}}$ — always.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The volume of the parallelepiped with co-terminous edges $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$, $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$, $\vec c=\hat k+\hat i$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec b\times\vec c=(1,1,-1)$; $\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=(1)(1)+(1)(1)+(0)(-1)=2$, so the volume is $2$.
questions.trick: Volume of a parallelepiped = scalar triple product $\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The angle between $\vec a = \hat i+\hat j$ and $\vec b = \hat j+\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 1$, $|\vec a|=|\vec b|=\sqrt2$, so $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$, giving $\theta = 60^\circ$.
questions.trick: $\cos\theta=(\vec a\cdot\vec b)/(|\vec a||\vec b|)$ — compute all three quickly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The magnitude of $\vec a = 3\hat i - 4\hat j + 12\hat k$ is
questions.trick: 3-4-12 form a Pythagorean-style triple: $\sqrt{9+16+144}=13$ instantly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $\vec a=2\hat i+\lambda\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k$ are perpendicular, then $\lambda=$
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=2-2\lambda+3=5-2\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac52$.
questions.trick: Perpendicular $\Rightarrow$ set the dot product to zero and solve for the unknown.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The unit vector along $3\hat i + 4\hat j$ is
questions.explanation: $|3\hat i+4\hat j| = \sqrt{9+16} = 5$, so the unit vector is $\dfrac{3\hat i+4\hat j}{5}$.
questions.trick: 3-4-5 triangle: magnitude is 5 instantly, so unit vector is $\vec a/5$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two planes $a_1x+b_1y+c_1z+d_1=0$ and $a_2x+b_2y+c_2z+d_2=0$ are parallel if
questions.explanation: Parallel planes have proportional normal vectors, i.e. proportional coefficients of $x,y,z$.
questions.trick: Parallel planes: coefficients of $x,y,z$ are proportional between the two equations.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The angle between the planes $x+y+2z=9$ and $2x-y+z=15$ is
questions.explanation: Normals $(1,1,2)$, $(2,-1,1)$: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{2-1+2}{\sqrt6\sqrt6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta=60^\circ$.
questions.trick: Angle between planes = angle between their normal vectors.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The direction cosines of a line that makes equal angles with all three coordinate axes are
questions.explanation: With $l=m=n$ and $l^2+m^2+n^2=1$, we get $3l^2=1 \Rightarrow l=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$.
questions.trick: Equal angles with all axes $\Rightarrow l=m=n=1/\sqrt3$ from $3l^2=1$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two parallel lines have direction ratios $(0,1,1)$ and pass through $(1,0,0)$ and $(1,1,0)$ respectively. The shortest distance between them is
questions.explanation: $\vec a_2-\vec a_1=(0,1,0)$; $\vec b\times(\vec a_2-\vec a_1) = (0,1,1)\times(0,1,0) = (-1,0,0)$, magnitude $1$; $|\vec b|=\sqrt2$, so $d=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$.
questions.trick: For parallel lines use $|\vec b\times(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)|/|\vec b|$, not the skew-line formula.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The plane $3x+4y-5z=60$ makes intercepts on the $x,y,z$ axes respectively equal to
questions.explanation: Dividing by 60: $\dfrac{x}{20}+\dfrac{y}{15}+\dfrac{z}{-12}=1$, so the intercepts are $20,15,-12$.
questions.trick: Divide by the RHS constant to read the intercepts off each denominator.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Lines with direction ratios $(2,-3,1)$ and $(-4,6,-2)$ are
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{-4}{2}=\dfrac{6}{-3}=\dfrac{-2}{1}=-2$, so the direction ratios are proportional and the lines are parallel.
questions.trick: Parallel lines: one set of DRs is a scalar multiple of the other.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The direction cosines of the line joining the origin and the point $(2,3,6)$ are
questions.explanation: The magnitude of $(2,3,6)$ is $\sqrt{4+9+36}=7$, so the direction cosines are $(2/7,3/7,6/7)$.
questions.trick: DCs of a point from the origin = its coordinates divided by its distance.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k)+t(\hat i-\hat j+\hat k)$ and $\vec r=(2\hat i-\hat j-\hat k)+s(2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec b_1\times\vec b_2=(-1,0,1)$, magnitude $\sqrt2$; $\vec a_2-\vec a_1=(1,-3,-2)$, whose dot product with $(-1,0,1)$ is $-3$. Shortest distance $=|-3|/\sqrt2=3/\sqrt2$.
questions.trick: Cross the two direction vectors first, then dot with the vector joining the lines.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The distance of the point $(2,3,-5)$ from the plane $x+2y-2z=9$ is
questions.trick: Substitute the point into the plane's LHS, divide by the normal's magnitude.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The planes $x+y+z=1$ and $x-2y+z=0$ are
questions.explanation: Normals $(1,1,1)$ and $(1,-2,1)$: $1-2+1=0$, so the planes are perpendicular.
questions.trick: Perpendicular planes: dot product of their normals equals zero.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The equation of the yz-plane is
questions.explanation: Every point on the yz-plane has its x-coordinate equal to zero.
questions.trick: The yz-plane is defined by $x=0$ for every point on it.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The equation of a plane making intercepts $a,b,c$ on the $x,y,z$ axes respectively is
questions.explanation: This is the standard intercept form of the equation of a plane.
questions.trick: Intercept form $x/a+y/b+z/c=1$ — read intercepts directly off the denominators.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The distance of the point $(1,1,1)$ from the plane $x+y+z-6=0$ is
questions.trick: Distance $=|ax_1+by_1+cz_1+d|/\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}$ — plug the point into the plane's LHS.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-3}{1}=\dfrac{y-k}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}$ intersect for $k=$
questions.explanation: Coplanarity requires $(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)\cdot(\vec d_1\times\vec d_2)=0$. With $\vec a_2-\vec a_1=(2,k+1,-1)$ and $\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=(-5,2,1)$, this gives $2k-9=0\Rightarrow k=9/2$.
questions.trick: Set the coplanarity determinant to zero and solve for the unknown parameter.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The angle between the lines with direction ratios $(1,1,0)$ and $(1,0,0)$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2\times1} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, so $\theta = 45^\circ$.
questions.trick: $\cos\theta=(a_1a_2+b_1b_2+c_1c_2)/(\text{magnitudes})$ — plug DRs directly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: For the constraints $x+y\le10$, $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, the point $(2,3)$ is
questions.explanation: Since $2+3=5\le10$ and both coordinates are non-negative, $(2,3)$ satisfies all constraints, so it is a feasible solution (though not a corner point).
questions.trick: Plug the point into every constraint; if all hold, it's feasible.

questions.q: Maximise $Z = 3x + 4y$ subject to $x+y\le4$, $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$. The maximum value of $Z$ is
questions.explanation: Corner points are $(0,0), (4,0), (0,4)$ with $Z = 0, 12, 16$ respectively; the maximum is $16$.
questions.trick: Evaluate $Z$ at every corner point; the largest is the maximum.

questions.q: If the only constraints on an LPP are $x\ge0$ and $y\ge0$ (no other restriction), the feasible region is
questions.explanation: With no upper bound on $x$ or $y$, every point in the first quadrant satisfies both constraints, so the feasible region is the whole (unbounded) first quadrant.
questions.trick: Only $x,y\ge0$ with no upper bound $\Rightarrow$ the whole first quadrant is feasible.

questions.q: Maximise $Z=x+2y$ subject to $x+y\le6$, $x,y\ge0$. The maximum of $Z$ occurs at the corner point
questions.explanation: $Z(0,6)=12$ is the largest among the corner values $0,6,12$.
questions.trick: Compare $Z$ values at each vertex; the biggest one wins.

questions.q: A firm makes chairs ($x$) and tables ($y$). Each chair needs 2 h of carpentry and 1 h of finishing; each table needs 1 h of carpentry and 2 h of finishing. Carpentry time available is 60 h and finishing time is 48 h per week. The correct constraints (besides $x,y\ge0$) are
questions.explanation: Total carpentry time used is $2x+y$, capped at 60 h; total finishing time used is $x+2y$, capped at 48 h.
questions.trick: Match each resource's total usage (coeff$\times x$+coeff$\times y$) to its available limit.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: The conditions $x\ge0, y\ge0$ in a linear programming problem are called the
questions.explanation: These conditions, required because decision variables usually represent quantities, are called non-negative restrictions.
questions.trick: $x\ge0,y\ge0$ are called non-negative restrictions, distinct from the other constraints.

questions.q: Consider minimising $Z=3x+2y$ subject to $x+y\ge8$, $3x+5y\le15$, $x,y\ge0$. This LPP has
questions.explanation: Along $x+y=8$ in the first quadrant, $3x+5y$ ranges from $24$ (at $(8,0)$) upward, always exceeding $15$; hence no point satisfies both constraints, so there is no feasible region.
questions.trick: If two constraints can't be satisfied together anywhere, there's no feasible solution.

questions.q: According to the Corner Point Theorem, if the feasible region of an LPP is bounded, the objective function attains its maximum and minimum at
options: the centroid of the feasible region
corner points of the feasible region
questions.explanation: The Corner Point Theorem states that for a bounded feasible region, the optimal values of a linear objective function occur at corner points (vertices).
questions.trick: Bounded region $\Rightarrow$ optimum always sits at a corner, never inside.

questions.q: Maximise $Z=3x+5y$ subject to $x+y\le2$, $3x+y\le3$, $x,y\ge0$. The maximum of $Z$ occurs at the corner point
questions.explanation: $Z(0,2)=10$ is the largest of the corner values $0,3,9,10$.
questions.trick: The corner giving the largest $Z$ is the answer — just compare, no shortcuts.

questions.q: Maximise $Z=3x+5y$ subject to $x+y\le2$, $3x+y\le3$, $x,y\ge0$. The maximum value of $Z$ is
questions.explanation: Corner points are $(0,0),(1,0),(0.5,1.5),(0,2)$ with $Z=0,3,9,10$; the maximum is $10$.

questions.q: A bag contains 4 white and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn one after another without replacement. The probability that both are black is
questions.explanation: $P=\dfrac{6}{10}\times\dfrac{5}{9}=\dfrac{30}{90}=\dfrac13$.
questions.trick: Without replacement: multiply successive fractions, denominator shrinks by 1 each draw.

questions.q: For a binomial distribution with $n=6$ and $p=1/3$, $P(X=0)$ is
questions.explanation: $P(X=0)={}^6C_0\left(\tfrac13\right)^0\left(\tfrac23\right)^6=\left(\tfrac23\right)^6=\dfrac{64}{729}$.
questions.trick: $P(X{=}0)$ for a binomial is just $q^n$ — no combinations needed.

questions.q: A die is thrown twice. The probability that the sum of the numbers is 9 given that at least one throw shows a 6 is
questions.explanation: At least one 6: 11 outcomes. Among them sum 9: (6,3) and (3,6) → $2/11$.
questions.trick: A condition narrows the sample space — count only outcomes meeting it, then find matches.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. The probability that the sum is 7 given that the first die shows 4 is
questions.explanation: Given the first die is 4, the second must be 3: probability $1/6$.
questions.trick: Given the first die's value, only the second die is uncertain — probability is $1/6$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A random variable $X$ takes values $0,1,2$ with probabilities $0.25,0.5,0.25$ respectively. The variance of $X$ is
questions.trick: Symmetric distribution: still compute $E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2$, don't skip the calculation.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are independent events with $P(A) = \dfrac13$ and $P(B) = \dfrac14$, then $P(A'\cap B')$ is
questions.explanation: $A', B'$ are also independent: $P(A')P(B') = \tfrac23\cdot\tfrac34 = \tfrac12$.
questions.trick: If $A,B$ independent, so are $A',B'$ — just multiply $P(A')\cdot P(B')$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack. Given that it is a face card, the probability that it is red is
questions.explanation: There are 12 face cards, of which 6 (hearts and diamonds) are red: $6/12=1/2$.
questions.trick: Half of all face cards are red (hearts $+$ diamonds) — ratio $6/12$.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A random variable $X$ has $P(X=1)=k$, $P(X=2)=2k$, $P(X=3)=3k$, $P(X=4)=4k$. Then $k$ and the variance of $X$ are
questions.explanation: $10k=1\Rightarrow k=0.1$. $E(X)=3$, $E(X^2)=10$, so variance $=10-9=1$.
questions.trick: Sum of $k$-multiples $=1$ gives $k$; then variance is $E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2$ as usual.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers is at least 10 is
questions.explanation: Sums of 10, 11, 12 occur in $3+2+1=6$ of the 36 outcomes, giving $6/36=1/6$.
questions.trick: Count favourable outcomes for sums 10, 11, 12 (3+2+1=6) out of 36.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Bag I has 2 red and 3 black balls; Bag II has 4 red and 1 black ball. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn from it is red. The probability that it came from Bag I is
questions.explanation: $P(\text{red})=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac25+\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac45=\tfrac15+\tfrac25=\tfrac35$. $P(\text{I}|\text{red})=\dfrac{1/5}{3/5}=\dfrac13$.
questions.trick: Bayes: compute $P(\text{red})$ via total probability first, then invert for the specific bag.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A fair die is thrown once. Given that the number shown is even, the probability that it is 4 is
questions.explanation: Given even, the sample space is $\{2,4,6\}$; the probability of getting 4 is $1/3$.
questions.trick: Given even, the reduced sample space is $\{2,4,6\}$ — pick the target from 3.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $P(A)=0.5$, $P(B)=0.3$ and $P(A\cap B)=0.15$, are $A$ and $B$ independent?
questions.explanation: $P(A)P(B)=0.5\times0.3=0.15=P(A\cap B)$, so $A$ and $B$ are independent.
questions.trick: Verify independence by checking if $P(A\cap B)$ equals $P(A)\times P(B)$ exactly.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: A machine produces defective items independently with probability 0.1. In a sample of 4 items, the probability that exactly 2 are defective is
questions.trick: Binomial with small $n$: plug straight into ${}^nC_rp^rq^{n-r}$, no shortcuts needed.

questions.q: A speaks the truth in 80% of cases and B in 75% of cases. The probability that they contradict each other in stating the same fact is
questions.explanation: $P = P(A_T)P(B_F) + P(A_F)P(B_T) = \tfrac45\cdot\tfrac14 + \tfrac15\cdot\tfrac34 = \tfrac{4 + 3}{20} = \tfrac7{20}$.
questions.trick: Contradiction $=$ (A true, B false) $+$ (A false, B true) — add the two products.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Bag I contains 3 red and 4 black balls; Bag II contains 5 red and 6 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn is red. The probability that it came from Bag II is
questions.explanation: $P(\text{II}|R) = \dfrac{\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac5{11}}{\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac37 + \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac5{11}} = \dfrac{5/11}{(33 + 35)/77} = \dfrac{5}{11}\times\dfrac{77}{68} = \dfrac{35}{68}$.
questions.trick: Bayes: (prior$\times$likelihood for II) over (sum across all bags of prior$\times$likelihood).
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: Three coins are tossed. The probability of getting at least two heads is
questions.explanation: Outcomes with 2 or 3 heads: 3 + 1 = 4 of 8.
questions.trick: List all 8 outcomes of 3 coins; count those with at least 2 heads.

questions.q: Two dice are thrown. Given that the sum of the numbers shown is even, the probability that both dice show the same number is
questions.explanation: Sum is even in 18 of 36 outcomes; among these, the 6 'doubles' outcomes (all of which have even sum) give both dice equal, so $P=6/18=1/3$.
questions.trick: Given sum even, doubles automatically qualify — count them among the even-sum outcomes.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: In a class, 60% are boys and 40% are girls. 5% of boys and 10% of girls score an A grade. If a randomly chosen student scored an A grade, the probability that the student is a girl is
questions.trick: Bayes: numerator is (group's prior $\times$ its rate); denominator sums both groups.
questions.subject: maths

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events with $P(A)=0.3$ and $P(B)=0.4$, then $P(A\cup B)$ is
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events, $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)=0.3+0.4=0.7$.
questions.trick: Mutually exclusive $\Rightarrow$ just add $P(A)+P(B)$, no subtraction needed.
